blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Ahmar (RA), the slave freed by Hazrat Umm Salamah (RA), narrates, “We were with Rasulullah ﷺ in a battle (and had to cross a stream or a river). At that time I was helping the people to cross the stream or river. Seeing this, the Prophet ﷺ looked at me and said, “Today you are nothing but a ship.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ ﵁ قَالَ: كُنَّا يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ كُلُّ ثَلَاثَةٍ عَلَي بَعِيرٍ قَالَ: فَكَانَ أَبُو لُبَابَةَ وَعَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ زَمِيلَيْ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ: فَكَانَتْ إِذَا جَاءَتْ عُقْبَةُ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَا: نَحْنُ نَمْشِي عَنْكَ، قَالَ: مَا أَنْتُمَا بِأَقْوَي مِنِّيْ وَمَا أَنَا بِأَغْنَي عَنِ اْلاَجْرِ مِنْكُمَا.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه البغوي في شرح السنة (اسناده حسن):١١ /٣٥
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) narrates, “At the Battle of Badr there was one camel for every three of us, and we would ride it in turns. Hazrat Abu Lubabah and Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) were both travelling companions on the camel of Rasulullah ﷺ”. Hazrat Abdullah (RA) says, “When the turn of Rasulullah ﷺ to walk came, Hazrat Abu Lubabah and Hazrat Ali (RA) would both say, “(Please keep riding the camel;) we will walk in your place.” The Prophet ﷺ would say, “Neither are you two stronger than me, nor am I less in need than you of good and reward.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ ﵄ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: سَيِّدُ الْقَوْمِ فِي السَّفَرِ خَادِمُهُمْ فَمَنْ سَبَقَهُمْ بِخِدْمَةٍ لَمْ يَسْبِقُوهُ بِعَمَلٍ إِلَّا
